title: Operational Debt & SLO Remediation: Sprint Plan (Q3 2026)
content:
Executive summary:

This note proposes a focused 6-week remediation sprint (Q3 2026) to attack operational debt causing SLO drift across model-serving and control-plane surfaces. The program bundles small, high-impact technical fixes, alert tuning, and playbook updates into a single cross-functional cadence so feature teams, platform, and SRE can make observable, measurable progress against reliability targets.

Why now:
- Multiple services show creeping SLO breaches related to noisy alerts, unaccounted error classes, and insufficient runbooks.
- Customer incidents in May/June highlighted gaps in rollback/runbook clarity for Dedicated and Hosted endpoints.
- We have bandwidth from Platform and Observability teams in July–Aug to collaborate.

Goals (outcomes, not outputs):
1) Reduce false-positive alert volume tied to SLO violations by >=40% for core model-serving routes (text-generation and embeddings) within 6 weeks.
2) Close or mitigate top 8 operational-debt items contributing to repeat incidents (see backlog).
3) Ensure every service with a customer-facing SLO has an updated runbook and postmortem template.
4) Automate error-budget burn alerts and attach remediation playbooks to the alert.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Alert noise metric (alerts/service/day) down by 40% from baseline (baseline taken 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-14).
- SLO violation rate for P99 latency on hosted text-generation routes reduced to under target threshold for 14 continuous days post-sprint (where achievable).
- 100% of services in scope have runbook with owner and a linked playbook in Confluence.
- Error budget auto-escalation configured for top-10 services.

Scope (in-scope vs out-of-scope):
- In-scope: hosted API frontend, routing layer, model-serving inference pool (GPU gateway), metrics/alerting config, runbooks for top 12 services by traffic.
- Out-of-scope: billing pipelines, long-term capacity rearchitecture, external partner integrations not affecting production SLOs.

High-level timeline (6 weeks):
- Week 0 (prework, 1 week): triage backlog, finalize scope, instrument measurement dashboards, baseline metrics.
- Weeks 1–4 (execution): parallel remediation tracks (observability, alert tuning, runbooks, infra quick fixes).
- Week 5 (validation & hardening): validate fixes in staging and canary, update dashboards, runbook walkthroughs with oncall.
- Week 6 (retro & handoff): cross-team post-sprint review, open followups, commit maintenance windows.

Sprint cadence and rituals:
- Weekly 60-minute triage sync (Mon 10am PT). Owners must bring a 2-line status and blockers.
- Twice-weekly focused working hours for Observability and Platform (Tue/Thu 2–4pm PT) to pair on alert rule changes and runbook tests.
- Daily async stand in #sre-ops with short check-ins for critical escalations.

Roles & RACI (high-level):
- Program owner: Alyssa Chen (SRE) — overall delivery, weekly sync lead.
- Platform SME: Diego Morales — infra fixes, deployment coordination.
- Observability lead: Priya Raman — dashboards, alert rules, instrumentation.
- Feature team liaisons: service owners (see backlog) — implement code-level fix/guardrails.
- QA/Validation: Owen Park — staging runchecks and canary validation.
- Documentation & runbooks: Samira Khan — runbook templates, linking to Confluence.

Workstreams and example tasks (each with estimated days):
1) Observability baseline and metric hardening (7–10d)
   - Audit existing SLI definitions for top 12 services (2d).
   - Add missing histograms/KV cache hit-rate metrics for model-serving (3d).
   - Implement per-route latency buckets for text-generation (2–3d).

2) Alert triage & tuning (5–8d)
   - Redefine alert thresholds tied to SLOs (panic vs warning) (2d).
   - Consolidate redundant alerts and add suppression for known transient classes (2d).
   - Add playbook links and required fields to alert payloads (1–2d).

3) Runbooks and playbooks (4–6d)
   - Create/update runbooks for each service: owner, rollback steps, relevant dashboards, and runbook test checklist (2–3d).
   - Runbook walkthrough with oncall and feature team (1d).

4) Quick infra remediations (6–9d)
   - Fix top 3 deployment hotpaths causing rollbacks to be slow (3d).
   - Add circuit-breaker adjustments and rate-limits to routing (2–3d).
   - Short-term autoscaler tuning for Dedicated pools to avoid warm-up spikes (1–3d).

5) Error-budget automation (3–5d)
   - Implement error-budget burn alerts that escalate to SRE when sustained (1d).
   - Link automated runbook and create Slack escalation path + PagerDuty overrides (1–2d).

6) Validation & canary testing (3–5d)
   - Canary test scenarios for latency and error-classes (2d).
   - Run chaos-lite (traffic skew) to validate suppression and circuit-breaker behavior (1–2d).

Sprint schedule (example week-by-week):
- Week 0 (2026-06-21 to 2026-06-27): backlog groom, baseline dashboards, pick owners, create ticket set.
- Week 1 (2026-06-28 to 2026-07-04): Observability audit + quick infra fixes priority 1.
- Week 2 (2026-07-05 to 2026-07-11): Alert tuning + runbook drafting.
- Week 3 (2026-07-12 to 2026-07-18): Continue infra fixes, begin error-budget automation.
- Week 4 (2026-07-19 to 2026-07-25): Validation, canary runs, oncall walkthroughs.
- Week 5 (2026-07-26 to 2026-08-01): Retro, handoff to feature teams for long-term items, schedule followups.

Backlog (top items to address):
- SRE-412: P99 latency alarms firing during model-variant swaps — investigation + mitigation.
- SRE-423: noisy 502s from routing layer when autoscaler spins up new GPUs.
- SRE-441: Missing KV-cache hit metrics for Llama-optim models.
- SRE-447: Runbooks not linked to alert payloads for dedicated capacity incidents.
- SRE-502: Circuit-breaker misfires causing cascade when backend slowdowns occur.

Dependencies and cross-team handoffs:
- Platform must schedule a maintenance window for rolling kernel upgrades (blocks infra quick fixes).
- Feature teams must review and merge instrumentation PRs within 3 working days of approval.
- Observability requires read access to model-serving telemetry namespaces — infra to grant.

Risk register (top 5):
- Risk: Change to alert thresholds hides real regressions. Mitigation: Pair threshold changes with short-term increased SLI sampling and a 72-hour review window.
- Risk: Quick infra fixes destabilize canary. Mitigation: Two-stage rollout + abort criteria and oncall in-loop.
- Risk: Feature teams miss review SLAs, blocking instrumentation. Mitigation: Blocker policy: escalate to engineering leads after 48 hours.

Open questions (to resolve in prework week):
- What is the canonical list of top-12 services by customer impact? (ops/product to finalize)
- Are there any regulatory constraints for logging or retention that affect new metrics? (legal/compliance)
- Can Platform guarantee two non-overlapping maintenance windows?

Communications plan:
- Weekly summary (one-pager) posted to #reliability-updates and SRE channel.
- End-of-sprint report delivered to Eng Leadership and Product with before/after metrics.

Next steps (immediately actionable):
1) Program kickoff + alignment meeting: Mon 2026-06-21 10am PT (invite sent).
2) Owners accept JIRA tickets and confirm availability by 2026-06-23.
3) Observability lead to publish baseline dashboards by 2026-06-25.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally scoped as a 6-week tactical burst to reduce noise and close small, high-value debt. Long-lived structural work (capacity redesign, major infra refactor) will be scheduled separately.
- Expect some tasks to slip; plan includes validation week to catch regressions.

Appendix (quick links & templates):
- Runbook template: Confluence /display/SRE/Runbook+Template
- Alert change checklist (must include rollback criteria): GitHub PR template link above.
- Example canary test plan (short): see attached playground in repo observability/tests/canary_scenarios.md
